subject: Dedicated reservation options and activation runway — Lattice Biotech
messages:
From: Sam Rogers <sam.rogers@latticebiotech.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2029-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — timeline and minimums

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this. We’re trying to firm up reserve options for Lattice Biotech for a new genomics inference pipeline. High level: production start target is the week of 2029-06-17, initial traffic expected ~10 qps peak (short bursts up to 25 qps), and cost is a major gating factor for Procurement.

Can you send over 2–3 reservation profiles that show:
- cluster size (GPU count),
- minimum guaranteed GPUs,
- suggested ramp schedule (weeks to reach baseline),
- warm-start / prewarm credit structure, and
- what graceful rollback or decommit options look like after month 3.

Also include any short-term burst/overage policies and a ballpark monthly committed price for each profile so Procurement can evaluate.

We have an internal procurement review on 2029-05-28, so a sheet this week would be ideal.

Best,
Sam
Sam Rogers
Head of Platform Engineering
Lattice Biotech

Attachments: none
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Rogers <sam.rogers@latticebiotech.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@latticebiotech.com>
Date: 2029-05-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — timeline and minimums

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a concise options workbook (reserve-options-lattice-20290520.xlsx) and a short PDF with the activation runway graphic. High-level summary below; I recommended calling out tradeoffs so Procurement can prioritize cost vs. headroom.

Option 1 — Starter slate (cost-focused)
- Cluster: 16 x A100-equivalent GPUs
- Minimum guarantee: 6 GPUs (soft floor)
- Ramp: can hit baseline (10 qps) in 2 weeks with aggressive pre-warm; suggested phased activation: canary -> 2-week scale
- Warm-start credits: 40k token-equivalent credit (reduces cold RTX for first 30 days)
- Overages: burst windows up to +50% for 6 hours/day at metered overage rate
- Ballpark committed price: $XXk/month (see spreadsheet)

Option 2 — Balanced onramp (recommended)
- Cluster: 64 GPUs (mixed precision, quantized-friendly)
- Minimum guarantee: 24 GPUs (hard floor)
- Ramp: 0–2 weeks canary (12 GPUs), weeks 3–6 scale to 24 GPUs, weeks 7–12 scale to 48–64 depending on traffic
- Warm-start credits: 150k token-equivalent + 2 pre-warm windows/month
- Overages: configurable burst lanes (up to 100% for short bursts at capped premium)
- Price: $YYk/month; includes 2 weeks of reduced-rate onboarding credits

Option 3 — Anchored throughput (enterprise readiness)
- Cluster: 128 GPUs
- Minimum guarantee: 48 GPUs (hard floor, SLA-backed)
- Ramp: canary 24 GPUs, 4–8 week staged ramp to full capacity; includes guaranteed prewarm and dedicated hot spares
- Warm-start credits: 400k token-equivalent, priority autoscale, and faster kernel tuning windows
- Price: $ZZk/month; SLA on latency percentiles

Decommit/rollback guidance (all options)
- 30-day notice to reduce guaranteed floor; pro-rated credits/penalties for earlier termination depending on committed term.

Next steps: if Procurement wants a single recommended path, our internal preference is Option 2 for a balance of cost and headroom. If you want, we can convert Option 2 into an executable SOW + DocuSign for signature.

I’ve copied a couple of folks on the Redwood side to confirm activation windows and potential canary cadence.

Cheers,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: reserve-options-lattice-20290520.xlsx, capacity-runway-graphs.pdf
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2029-05-20T13:25:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity ask — timeline and minimums

Folks — forwarding Sam's ask and my draft options (see attached). Procurement will review next week; I suggested Option 2 as our recommended path. A few open items I want us aligned on before I send the formal proposal:

1) Canary sizing: propose an initial 2-week canary at 12 GPUs with traffic shaping and tracing hooks. Is 12 GPUs enough to validate end-to-end latency and model quality?
2) Pricing mechanics: can we offer a stepped discount for months 2–3 if they commit to a 12-month term? Suggest 7.5% off list in months 2–6, then standard reserved pricing thereafter.
3) Warm-start credit accounting: how strictly do we meter token-equivalent credits vs. time-boxed pre-warm windows?
4) SLA escape hatch: propose an operational rollback allowing them to reduce floor by 50% after month 3 with a 30-day notice and a modest rebalancing fee.

Please reply with short bullets — Procurement appreciates clean, binary choices.

— Mina

[Attachment: reserve-options-lattice-20290520.xlsx]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2029-05-21T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity ask — timeline and minimums

Short answers:
1) 12 GPUs for the canary is fine if we limit sequence lengths and use aggressive caching; plan to capture KV hit rates and tail latency.
2) Agree on stepped discount; 7.5% months 2–6, 3% months 7–12 is conservative but defensible.
3) Meter credits as token-equivalent but also provide 2 fixed pre-warm windows per month (helps them schedule heavy unseen loads).
4) Rollback: allow 50% reduction after month 3 with a one-time rebalancing fee equal to 10% of one month's committed spend (covers provisioning churn).

I'll tweak the numbers in the proposal PDF.

— Ben
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2029-05-23T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — timeline and minimums

Hi Sam / team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on Procurement's ask and internal alignment, attached is the recommended plan and a compact SOW (lattice-proposal-20290523.pdf). Summary of the recommended path and activation runway:

Recommended: Option 2 (Balanced onramp) — executed as a 12-month commitment with a 60-day staged activation runway.
Activation runway (detailed):
- Week 0–2 (Canary): 12 GPUs active, focused traffic shaping and tracing; 2-week verification window.
- Week 3–6 (Phase 1): scale to 24 GPUs; enable 1st burst lane (short, capped).
- Week 7–12 (Phase 2): scale to 48 GPUs and activate automated batching/caching profile tuned for your request distribution.
- Month 4+: evaluate metrics (p99 latency, cost per token); option to increase to 64 GPUs if sustained 20% headroom needed.

Commercials:
- Committed price: see PDF (sheet summary). We've applied a 7.5% stepped onboarding discount months 2–6 and a 3% term discount months 7–12 for a total blended onboarding concession.
- Warm-starts: 150k token-equivalent credits + 2 scheduled pre-warm windows/month.
- Rollback: after month 3, Lattice may reduce guaranteed floor by up to 50% with 30 days' notice; a one-time rebalancing fee equal to 10% of one month's committed spend applies.

Next steps:
1) I can open a DocuSign envelope with the SOW; signing will lock the 12-month reserved pricing and onboarding credits. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.net/embeddedSigning/abcdef123456
2) If Procurement wants a small canary contract amendment instead of full SOW, we can provide a 6-week pilot addendum.

If that looks good I’ll send the DocuSign formally and schedule a kickoff for week of 2029-06-10 to coordinate pre-warm windows and tracing hooks.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
